title: Digital Agriculture Maturity Model
ratification_note: Twelve design decisions are open in specification section 13. Every value they can change is data in this file. A consumer must not present an unratified value as settled: see `open_decisions` for which fields each ruling governs.
prohibitions: No band used as a project development objective, disbursement-linked indicator or disbursement condition.
No public claim before human review.

config.rounding_note: Half-up to 2dp, matching the workbook. Banker's rounding disagrees at exact .xx5 and would band a mean differently.

A1.name: Agriculture & need
A1.note: Scored as need, not digital maturity: a low reading is a large opportunity.

non_use_case_tags.NEED: Bears on the agricultural-need profile, not on a use-case column.
non_use_case_tags.AI: Binds AI-enabled services; loop-1 ruling binds it to AGI pending a definition (13.4).

evidence_classes.derived_from: a non-numeric value with a source at an admissible tier (not T5)
evidence_classes.levels: assessor level against the shared qualitative ladder

evidence_classes.derived_from: a non-numeric value with no source, or a T5-only citation
the value records a search trail beginning 'DATA GAP'
evidence_classes.levels: none — a gap is never levelled

source_tiers.T5: News and vendor material — existence facts only; never yields Documented

tier_note: Tiers are reported, never weighted. Weighting them would rebuild the confidence weights v1.6 removed.

prerequisite_kinds.UC:<list>: Absence blocks the named columns only.
prerequisite_kinds.DELIVERY: Delivery-risk flag. Reported on the cover; blocks nothing.

prerequisite_status.Unverified: no level recorded — an unrated row asserts nothing, and is never Absent

binding_rules.rule: Any universal prerequisite Absent -> every column Blocked.
Any universal prerequisite Unverified -> every column Unverified. A known blocker outranks an unknown one.
Any universal prerequisite at Present (narrow) -> every column capped at Partial.
A per-use-case prerequisite Absent -> that column Blocked; Unverified -> that column Unverified.
7.12 (consent and rights) binds every use case drawing on personal or farm-level data. The column set is a 13.3 mapping question and is not ratified.
binding_rules.note: The external review argues this should condition every use case touching personal or farm-level data rather than block one column.

binding_rules.rule: Mean of bearing indicators below the readiness threshold -> Partial.
binding_rules.note: The bearing set mixes need, outcome and enabling indicators. See open decision 13.12.

invariants: No level without a recorded value; the evidence class is derived from what was recorded, never chosen.
A withheld level is not an absence. A prerequisite so recorded reads Unverified, never Absent.
A mean averages rated rows only, and never travels without its own denominator (rated of n).
No narrative claim ever sets a level.

ratification.open_question: The name says "Agriculture... (USD)" but both countries record WDI NV.AGR.EMPL.KD, which covers agriculture, forestry AND fishing and is denominated in constant 2015 US$ — neither the sector scope nor the price basis is stated in the name or in the bare-USD thresholds, and neither row carries…

The name omits the denominator (% of total employment), the recorded series covers ISIC-A (agriculture, hunting, forestry and fishing) rather than agriculture alone, and both rows carry an ILO MODELLED 2025 nowcast under cls "Measured" — the register's highest evidence class — which the…

The name asserts an all-crop national post-harvest loss rate; both countries record cereals-only figures, and Egypt's scored figure is described by its own source as covering pre- AND post-harvest losses.

The name asserts national smallholder ACCESS to formal markets; Egypt records a regional contract-farming PARTICIPATION rate from seven governorates and Nigeria a 2012/13 channel-of-sale share — two different constructs, neither of which is access, and neither national in Egypt's case.

The name asserts a share of FARMERS with credit ACCESS; Egypt records rural adults aged 15+ (a population that includes non-farmers) and Nigeria records smallholder households, and both measure borrowing/use rather than access.

The name counts FARMERS adopting climate-smart practices; Egypt records a share of WHEAT AREA under a single practice and Nigeria a share of farmers in two zones adopting at least one climate-resilient crop TRAIT — land, practice-basket and geographic scope all differ from the name.

absorbs.name: Rural population covered by at least 4G (%)

ratification.open_question: The name asserts RURAL coverage, but Egypt's row records the ITU national at-least-3G figure as a clean cls="Measured" number that scores level 5 mechanically, while Nigeria records a rural-but-4G-only modelled estimate — so the register's only universal connectivity prerequisite carries a…

absorbs.name: Active mobile broadband subscriptions per 100 inhabitants

ratification.open_question: The name fixes neither the basket allowance (2GB vs ITU's 2025 headline 5GB), nor the basket type (data-only vs voice+data), nor whether "% GNI pc" is monthly or annual — and Egypt's value sits on a series ITU has retired to a legacy label while Nigeria's comes from the live headline series id,…

absorbs.name: Adults with mobile phone (% age 15+)

ratification.open_question: "Ownership" of a personal device implies individuals; both countries record the share of rural HOUSEHOLDS owning at least one smartphone, which reads systematically higher than the individual measure.

The ladder's name fixes neither a targeting test nor whether a subsidy is required, and the two countries applied opposite tests to the same class of evidence — commercial telco handset instalments — producing a two-rung divergence.

The name implies a register of farmers (individuals), but Egypt's record is an agricultural holding registry embedded in a subsidy smart-card scheme, whose scale figures mix four non-comparable units — cards printed, cards distributed, farmers benefiting, and holdings registered — with no…

The name reads as one object but three distinct registers are in play — legal title, a national all-property real-estate ID database, and agricultural usufruct/holding records — and Egypt's rung-3 anchor is an economy-wide real-estate identification law (urban property included) scored inside an…

absorbs.name: Machine-readable open agricultural data (share as open APIs)
AI-ready agricultural datasets

ratification.open_question: The name asserts three conjoined qualifiers — open, machine-readable, AI-ready — and Nigeria scores rung 4 ('Operating with quality') on a registration-gated statistical microdata catalogue that the cell's own text says is neither open nor AI-ready, while Nigeria's actual open-data portals are…

The name is data infrastructure — observation networks, archives, data access — but both countries are scored at rung 4 on advisory products issued to farmers, with no station density, archive, API or data-access evidence recorded on either row, and the advisory content overlaps indicator 8.17…

The name fixes neither the object nor the bar for 'integration' — Egypt is scored rung 4 on producing national crop maps, Nigeria rung 3 on institutional arrangements — and Egypt's 'operating beyond pilots' assertion rests on a source whose own title announces a pilot launch, recorded under year…
Does a digitised legacy paper soil map satisfy the indicator, or does the ladder measure an operating digital soil information service?

"At scale" fixes no threshold anywhere in the model (th=[] for all ladder rows), so a >10k-user bar imported from outside the audited files carries both level 4s, and the counts behind it are self-reported registered users rather than active or reached farmers.
Does the indicator count only farmer-facing platforms, or any agri-food value-chain commerce platform (OneOrder, Cartona, AFEX)?
Must the standard be agriculture-specific, or do cross-government open-data/DPI instruments and draft harmonisation work count as Present/Announced for this prerequisite cell?

Thresholds are defined on a 0–1 basis but Egypt is recorded as 100 and Nigeria as 0.824, so the same register column holds two incommensurable scales; separately, neither number is an overall score ITU actually publishes in the GCI 2024 report.
Now that the 2025 edition dropped the open overall score, does the cell score the stale 2024 overall score, substitute rank plus pillar scores, or gap?

Does the indicator score only a dedicated digital-agriculture strategy document, or does it credit digital-ag components embedded in broader national strategies and active programmes running without a strategy?

absorbs.name: Data sovereignty provisions for agricultural data

indicators.name: National AI strategy with agriculture component

absorbs.name: Responsible AI principles/guidelines for agriculture

ratification.open_question: What evidence makes a strategy 'Adopted' — official publication, or formal executive/cabinet approval?

The name asserts a digital ID, but Egypt records the World Bank ID4D foundational national-ID-card ownership series while ID4D's actual digital-ID series exists and was not used — and on top of that the two countries are recorded on different denominators (Egypt % of adults 15+, Nigeria % of…
Does the indicator require a formally constituted standing body or committee, or does any documented recurring — including project-based — coordination mechanism satisfy it?

The name asserts the STEM subset of tertiary enrolment, but both countries record World Bank WDI SE.TER.ENRR, which is total tertiary gross enrolment across all fields, and the level is then scored against thresholds calibrated for a STEM share.

The name asserts a national digital-literacy rate among farmers, but Nigeria records rural-population digital skills and Egypt records a two-governorate RCT baseline whose headline figure is digital ILliteracy, the inverse of the indicator's H direction.

absorbs.name: National innovation/extension programs with digital component
Farmer-to-digital-extension-worker ratio
Institutional digital maturity of key agricultural agencies

ratification.open_question: The name asserts a standing digital/AI unit inside the ministry of agriculture, but Egypt is scored level 3 on a joint MALR-MCIT programme while the row's own note records that the named unit could not be confirmed and that the prior evidence for it was ruled inadmissible — and because this row…

absorbs.name: Data science/AI training programs for agriculture

ratification.open_question: The name's "agtech" half is unevidenced in both countries — each level 3 is carried entirely by a generic national ICT/data-talent programme with the agriculture bridging explicitly absent — and the slash never says whether the two halves are conjunctive or disjunctive.

absorbs.name: Gender parity in extension services

ratification.open_question: Who counts as the 'digital-ag workforce' — extension staff, agtech-company employees, or ICT-in-agriculture roles generally — given the H 20/35/45/50 thresholds presuppose a share no source publishes?

absorbs.name: Venture capital/investment in agtech
Agtech accelerators/incubators
Government grants/funding for agtech innovation

ratification.open_question: The scale evidence is AgFunder "agrifoodtech" deal flow, a category that includes downstream food-tech and non-farmer-facing ventures, standing in for an agtech venture ecosystem — a measurably broader denominator that inflates deal and funding counts.

The name asserts operating public-private partnerships, but Nigeria's level 3 rests substantially on MOUs signed days before capture (intent, not operation) and Egypt's flagship partnership pairs ministries with state-owned financial entities, leaving the "private" half of the construct thin.
Does 'DPG adopted' mean the country deploying a globally registered DPG, or the country itself adopting a DPG policy or registering a national product?

absorbs.name: Agribusiness firms using AI/ML in operations (%)

ratification.open_question: The name fixes neither the population (SMEs economy-wide or agribusiness firms specifically — the slash is undefined) nor what counts as a "digital tool", and the register itself records that the available evidence cannot be mapped onto it.

absorbs.name: Digital financial services platforms for agriculture

ratification.open_question: The name asserts rails serving smallholders, but the scale evidence is instruments issued and vendor-reported farmers "reached" rather than active use, and Egypt's Farmer Card is a state-issued instrument for registered landholders generally rather than for smallholders specifically.

absorbs.name: AI-enabled advisory services (farmer reach)
AI for crop/pest/disease detection and monitoring
AI in agricultural finance (credit scoring, insurance)
AI for supply chain optimization and traceability
AI for climate forecasting and agricultural risk management

ratification.open_question: The name asserts deployment, but Egypt's level 3 rests on a solution restricted to a pilot cohort with no verified reach and Nigeria's row is anchored on a future-tense announcement of an intent to deploy.

absorbs.name: Explainability and transparency of AI systems in ag
Bias monitoring and mitigation in agricultural AI

ratification.open_question: The name does not fix whether the safeguards must be agriculture- or farmer-specific or whether a cross-sector regime suffices, and the two countries resolve it in opposite directions on the same recorded fact pattern — each row states that nothing agriculture-specific exists, yet one is scored…

absorbs.name: Gender gap in account ownership (male % minus female %)

ratification.open_question: "Account" is not defined in the name, and the chosen WDI series counts mobile-money accounts inside the total — the same construct scored separately at 8.4 — so mobile money is effectively double-weighted in the FIN use-case column and in the O1 mean.
The indicator name says women who OWN land while the canonical statistic counts women agricultural holders (operators), who may rent rather than own.

The name fixes the unit as percentage points but not the sign convention or the basis, so a reversed gap (women ahead) scores as best-in-class under direction L, and the widely quoted GSMA figure for the same construct is a relative gap on a male-ownership base, a different number entirely.

absorbs.name: Women using digital agricultural services
Youth using digital agricultural services
Gender-disaggregated adoption of digital advisories

ratification.open_question: The name asserts a national share of smallholders reached, but Egypt's scored level 1 is derived from a two-governorate RCT baseline explicitly labelled as having no national provenance, and "reached" is nowhere defined against registered, active, or benefiting users.

Should 8.11 remain a %-share indicator when no country publishes a denominator for local-language service delivery — and the Nigeria bundle's guidance text is contaminated with Egypt-specific content that must be removed regardless of the ruling?

absorbs.name: Documented income improvement from digital tools

ratification.open_question: The name's parenthetical fixes the outcome as yield or income, but Egypt's level 3 rests on an evaluation whose measured outcome is diffusion and adoption of digital tools, not yield or income.

absorbs.name: Farmers using digital climate services

ratification.open_question: Does the indicator measure farmer receipt of advisories, or supply-side issuance (warnings issued, platforms live), which is all either country publishes?

derived_sources.pillar_profile: Per-pillar mean, band, rated/held denominators and evidence composition.
derived_sources.leapfrog: Foundation minus Transformation, and the structural flag.
derived_sources.matrix: The six use-case readiness columns with both means.
derived_sources.prerequisites: Presence status of the twelve prerequisite rows.
derived_sources.constraints: Lowest-level rated indicators, the binding-constraint list.
derived_sources.kpi_baseline: Measured A1/O1 rows carried as baseline readings.
derived_sources.register: The initiative and solutions register, tier-badged.
derived_sources.evidence_ledger: Every row with class, level, source, tier, year; gaps, holds and stale readings.
derived_sources.foresight.scenarios: Scenario set produced by the foresight stage.
derived_sources.foresight.milestones: Backcast milestones and their indicator bindings.

dar_outline.title: Country and sector context
dar_outline.content: Agricultural structure, need and climate exposure; the national digital context the roadmap has to work inside.
dar_outline.note: A1 reads as NEED: a low reading is a large opportunity, never low maturity.

dar_outline.title: Where the country stands
dar_outline.content: Pillar and layer profiles with their rated denominators; the use-case readiness matrix; prerequisite status; the structural gap; what the evidence rests on.
dar_outline.note: This chapter is the diagnostic. Every figure must reconcile with the diagnostic report generated for the same assessment.

dar_outline.title: Vision, targeting and beneficiaries
dar_outline.content: Priority value chains, regions and farmer segments; which use cases are worth pursuing first, and for whom.
dar_outline.note: Targeting rests on the readiness matrix; beneficiary claims rest on A1 need and O1 equity rows. The vision itself comes from the foresight stage, not from the model.

dar_outline.title: The investment program
dar_outline.content: Sequenced candidates with dependencies and implementation owners; what has to be built before what.
dar_outline.note: Sequencing follows the prerequisites: a Blocked column names what must be built. A blocked use case is an argument FOR investment, never against it.

dar_outline.title: Costs and financing
dar_outline.content: Costed program under envelope scenarios; instrument routing; financing sources.
dar_outline.note: DAMM CARRIES NO COST, BUDGET OR FINANCING DATA OF ANY KIND. No figure in this chapter may be presented as derived from the model or the assessment. The only quantities available are scale figures as reported by initiatives in the register, which are the initiatives' own claims and are tier-badged as such.

dar_outline.title: Policy and regulatory actions
dar_outline.content: Reform actions arising from the policy and safeguards pillar; legal drafting needs.
dar_outline.note: An Absent prerequisite here is a named legal or regulatory instrument that does not exist; say which, and cite the row.

dar_outline.title: Delivery and governance
dar_outline.content: Mandate and ownership; steering arrangements; the institutional home and its capacity.
dar_outline.note: 4.9 and 5.7 are DELIVERY-risk flags: they are reported and they block nothing. Do not render them as gating anything.

dar_outline.title: Climate alignment
dar_outline.content: Climate-smart practice, advisory reach and the weather and climate data base the roadmap can build on.
dar_outline.note: The model holds no NDC or CCDR crosswalk and no climate-finance taxonomy. Alignment claims against those instruments are external and must be marked as such.

dar_outline.title: Results and learning
dar_outline.content: Results chains with baselines; the measurement gap register; what will be watched and how often.
dar_outline.note: Baselines come from Measured A1/O1 rows only. Recorded gaps, held levels and stale readings ARE the measurement gap register — carry them, do not summarise them away.

dar_outline.title: Risks and safeguards
dar_outline.content: Data rights, consent and redress; evidence-quality risk; political-economy risk and mitigations.
dar_outline.note: Evidence quality is itself a risk and belongs here: how much of the assessment rests on withheld levels, recorded gaps, stale readings and unratified definitions.

dar_outline.title: Annexes
dar_outline.content: The full indicator evidence base; the source and tier record; the open-decision register; the version and configuration record.
dar_outline.note: The annex is the audit trail. Nothing is summarised here; rows appear in full.

foresight.method: scenarios -> preferred future -> backcasting to milestones

steps.name: Scenarios
steps.purpose: Bound the uncertainty: plausible futures for the sector, not forecasts.

steps.name: Preferred future
steps.purpose: The normative selection — what the country would choose to bring about. A claim about values, not evidence, and marked as such.

steps.name: Backcasting to milestones
steps.purpose: Work back from the preferred future to dated, measurable milestones.

milestone_binding.rule: Each milestone binds to one or more indicators or prerequisites with a target level and a target year, so progress is measurable against the same instrument that produced the diagnostic.
milestone_binding.fallback: Where no indicator in the model fits, the milestone proposes a CANDIDATE indicator (see candidate_indicators) and binds to that instead.
milestone_binding.provisionality: A target level standing on an unratified threshold inherits that provisionality and carries the marking of the open decision governing it.

foresight.note: Where a foresight document is supplied it is ingested and this exercise is skipped. A machine-run preferred future is a facilitation input, never a finding.

candidate_indicators.purpose: Let a metric be recorded and carried without silently expanding the scored model.
candidate_indicators.disposition: Recorded, carried beside the assessment, flagged as a ratification item. Promotion to a scored indicator is a versioned model change, never automatic.

open_decisions.title: Band edges
open_decisions.ruled: Recut to midpoint boundaries. The band is the level the pillar mean rounds to, and a signed margin from that level is printed beside it.

open_decisions.title: A1 additions (cereal import dependency, irrigation)
open_decisions.ruled: Hold A1 at ten indicators. Both candidates stay carried and unscored, outside every mean, every prerequisite and the readiness matrix.

open_decisions.title: The three binding rules in force
open_decisions.ruled: Approved, with one change: 7.12 follows the use of personal or farm-level data rather than the agricultural-intelligence column alone. Which columns those are is a mapping question under 13.3 and is not ratified.

open_decisions.title: Sub-readings display
open_decisions.ruled: Nest beneath the parent row as unscored detail. Names for the 30 absorbed sub-readings were recovered from the v1.5 workbook; they carry no level and enter no mean.

open_decisions.title: Source-tier lookup and register field set
open_decisions.ruled: Approved subject to the qualifications: openknowledge.worldbank.org is T2 rather than T1; UN statistical hosts are T1 and the UN newswire is T5; a national statistical office with documented quality concerns is demoted row by row, never in bulk; a donor project completion report is T2 only if independently evaluated, otherwise T4.

open_decisions.title: QC gate scope
open_decisions.ruled: Approved subject to the qualifications, including the section 14 amendment: peer review must ask whether the evidence answers THIS indicator, not only whether the source states the number. The vendor audition measured why: quote verification caught every fabrication and no construct substitution at all.

open_decisions.title: Bhutan out of scope (statement)
open_decisions.ruled: Confirmed. Bhutan remains a design source and no assessment ships.

open_decisions.title: Whether need and outcome indicators belong in a readiness mean
open_decisions.ruled: Separate the three roles. A use-case column reads on its enabling indicators alone; need and outcome are reported beside it and never averaged into it.
